source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 2 (book page 205): periods of 11 functions, parts (i)-(xi). Answer key PDF 309 prints 2pi/3 for (i) and 40/pi for (v); correct values 2pi/5 and 40. Solution book PDF 996-1003.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find the periods of the following functions: \(\sin 5x\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a sine function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of sine (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sin 5x\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: sine, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = 5\]
Why: The angle \(5x\) runs 5 times as fast as \(x\), so one full turn of \(2\pi\) in the angle needs only \(2\pi/5\) in \(x\).

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\sin 5\left(x + \dfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)\]
\[= \sin(5x + 2\pi)\]
\[= \sin 5x\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(2\pi\) to the angle, and sine repeats after \(2\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(2\pi\) is the smallest period of sine.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) for part (i). This is a misprint: the coefficient of \(x\) in \(\sin 5x\) is 5, so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{5}\). (\(2\pi/3\) would be the period of \(\sin 3x\).)

blocks.explanation:

Plan: take the basic period of cosine (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: cosine, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = 7\]
Why: Cosine repeats after \(2\pi\), just like sine; the 7 makes it repeat 7 times as often.

Divide the basic period by \(c\)

Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

\[\cos 7\left(x + \dfrac{2\pi}{7}\right)\]

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find the periods of the following functions: \(\tan 3x\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a tangent function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of tangent (\(\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \tan 3x\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: tangent, basic period \(\pi\).
\[c = 3\]
Why: Tangent repeats after \(\pi\), not \(2\pi\) (Theorem 11.2), so we divide \(\pi\) by 3.

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\tan 3\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\]
\[= \tan(3x + \pi)\]
\[= \tan 3x\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(\pi\) to the angle, and tangent repeats after \(\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(\pi\) is the smallest period of tangent.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Find the periods of the following functions: \(\cot \frac{x}{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a cotangent function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of cotangent (\(\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \cot \frac{x}{2}\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: cotangent, basic period \(\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: Here \(c = 1/2\) is less than 1, so the graph is stretched and the period becomes longer than \(\pi\).

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = \pi \div \dfrac{1}{2}\]
\[= \pi \times 2 = 2\pi\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\cot \dfrac{x + 2\pi}{2}\]
\[= \cot\left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \pi\right)\]
\[= \cot \dfrac{x}{2}\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(\pi\) to the angle, and cotangent repeats after \(\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(\pi\) is the smallest period of cotangent.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Find the periods of the following functions: \(19\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{20}x\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a sine function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of sine (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 19\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{20}x\right)\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: sine, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{\pi}{20}\]
Why: The 19 only makes the wave taller (amplitude 19); it does not change how often it repeats. The \(\pi\) in \(c\) cancels the \(\pi\) of \(2\pi\), so the period is the plain number 40.

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{\pi}{20}\]
\[= 2\pi \times \dfrac{20}{\pi}\]
\[= 40\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{\pi}{20}(x + 40) = \dfrac{\pi x}{20} + 2\pi\]
\[19\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{20} + 2\pi\right) = 19\sin\dfrac{\pi x}{20}\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(2\pi\) to the angle, and sine repeats after \(2\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(2\pi\) is the smallest period of sine.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\frac{40}{\pi}\) for part (v). This is wrong: \(2\pi \div \frac{\pi}{20} = 40\); the two \(\pi\)'s cancel. Check: adding \(40\) to \(x\) adds \(\frac{\pi}{20} \times 40 = 2\pi\) to the angle, while adding \(\frac{40}{\pi}\) adds only \(2\) radians. The period is \(40\).

blocks.prompt: 2 (vi) Find the periods of the following functions: \(\operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{2x}{5}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a cosecant function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of cosecant (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \operatorname{cosec}\left(\frac{2x}{5}\right)\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: cosecant, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{2}{5}\]
Why: Cosecant is \(1/\sin\), so it repeats exactly when sine repeats: basic period \(2\pi\).

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{2}{5}\]
\[= 2\pi \times \dfrac{5}{2} = 5\pi\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{2}{5}(x + 5\pi) = \dfrac{2x}{5} + 2\pi\]
\[\operatorname{cosec}\left(\dfrac{2x}{5} + 2\pi\right) = \operatorname{cosec}\dfrac{2x}{5}\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(2\pi\) to the angle, and cosecant repeats after \(2\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(2\pi\) is the smallest period of cosecant.

blocks.prompt: 2 (vii) Find the periods of the following functions: \(\frac{1}{2}\sin\left(\frac{3x}{2} - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a sine function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of sine (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}\sin\left(\frac{3x}{2} - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: sine, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{3}{2}\]
Why: The \(\tfrac12\) in front (height) and the \(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) inside (a sideways shift) do not change the period; only the coefficient \(3/2\) of \(x\) matters.

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = 2\pi \div \dfrac{3}{2}\]
\[= 2\pi \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{3}{2}\left(x + \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3x}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2\pi\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(2\pi\) to the angle, and sine repeats after \(2\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(2\pi\) is the smallest period of sine.

blocks.prompt: 2 (viii) Find the periods of the following functions: \(-5 - 3\sec\left(7\pi x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a secant function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of secant (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = -5 - 3\sec\left(7\pi x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: secant, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = 7\pi\]
Why: Secant is \(1/\cos\), basic period \(2\pi\). The \(-5\), the \(-3\) and the \(+\pi/4\) do not affect the period. Here \(c = 7\pi\) contains \(\pi\), so the period has no \(\pi\).

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = \dfrac{2\pi}{7\pi}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{7}\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[7\pi\left(x + \dfrac{2}{7}\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\]
\[= 7\pi x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2\pi\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(2\pi\) to the angle, and secant repeats after \(2\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(2\pi\) is the smallest period of secant.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ix) Find the periods of the following functions: \(12 + 10\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{30}x\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a tangent function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of tangent (\(\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 12 + 10\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{30}x\right)\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). For \(a + b\,\mathrm{T}(cx + d)\) the period is (basic period)\(/|c|\); here T stands for the trigonometric function, and the numbers \(a\), \(b\) and \(d\) do not change the period.

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: tangent, basic period \(\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{\pi}{30}\]
Why: Tangent: basic period \(\pi\). The 12 and the 10 do not change the period.

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
\[\text{Period} = \pi \div \dfrac{\pi}{30}\]
\[= \pi \times \dfrac{30}{\pi} = 30\]
Why: the angle must grow by one basic period; since the angle grows \(c\) times as fast as \(x\), \(x\) needs only (basic period)\(/c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{\pi}{30}(x + 30) = \dfrac{\pi x}{30} + \pi\]
\[\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{30} + \pi\right) = \tan\dfrac{\pi x}{30}\]
Why: adding the period to \(x\) adds exactly \(\pi\) to the angle, and tangent repeats after \(\pi\). No smaller positive number works, because \(\pi\) is the smallest period of tangent.

blocks.prompt: 2 (x) Find the periods of the following functions: \(6 - 4\cot\left(\frac{7x}{4} + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:

Plan: take the basic period of cotangent (\(\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:

To find: the period of \(f\).

Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: cotangent, basic period \(\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{7}{4}\]
Why: Cotangent: basic period \(\pi\). Only the coefficient \(7/4\) of \(x\) matters.

Divide the basic period by \(c\)

blocks.prompt: 2 (xi) Find the periods of the following functions: \(9 + 30\sec\left(\frac{x}{15} + \frac{2\pi}{15}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
The function is a secant function; we must find the smallest positive \(p\) with \(f(x + p) = f(x)\).
Plan: take the basic period of secant (\(2\pi\)), read the coefficient \(c\) of \(x\), divide, then check.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 9 + 30\sec\left(\frac{x}{15} + \frac{2\pi}{15}\right)\).
To find: the period of \(f\).
Method: \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\) have basic period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\), \(\cot\) have basic period \(\pi\). Identify the function and \(c\)
Function: secant, basic period \(2\pi\).
\[c = \dfrac{1}{15}\]
Why: Here \(c = 1/15\) is very small, so the graph is stretched a lot and the period is long: \(30\pi\).

Divide the basic period by \(c\)
